instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 4111.03 Overtime
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime at one and one-half times the wage rate for hours over 40 in one workweek, in the manner and subject to the exemptions of FLSA sections 7 and 13 and Portal-to-Portal Act sections 2 and 4 (no daily overtime). Minimum-wage poster (US-OHS5-004) states the overtime duty does not apply to employers grossing less than 150,000 USD per year.

instrument_name: Ohio Department of Commerce 2027 Minimum Wage poster
authority: Ohio Department of Commerce, Wage & Hour
article_or_section: poster (Ohio Const. art. II s.34a; ORC 4111)
figure_or_rule_carried: 2027: non-tipped 11.40 USD/h; tipped 5.70 USD/h plus tips (tipped = customarily and regularly more than 30 USD/month in tips); employers grossing less than 419,000 USD and employees under 16 at the federal minimum 7.25 USD; overtime 1.5x over 40 h/week except employers grossing less than 150,000 USD/year; records kept 3 years (name, address, occupation, rate, amount paid per period, hours per day and week); exemptions incl. federal employees, babysitters in employer home, live-in companions, outside sales, EAP and computer professionals.

instrument_name: Ohio Department of Commerce 2026 Minimum Wage poster
authority: Ohio Department of Commerce, Wage & Hour
article_or_section: poster (Ohio Const. art. II s.34a; ORC 4111)
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026: non-tipped 11.00 USD/h; tipped 5.50 USD/h plus tips (more than 30 USD/month in tips); employers grossing less than 405,000 USD and employees under 16: federal 7.25 USD; overtime 1.5x over 40 h except employers grossing under 150,000 USD/year; records 3 years. Derivation: 10.70 (2025) x CPI-W Aug2025/Aug2024 (317.306/308.640) = 11.0004 -> 11.00 at nearest 5 cents; tipped = 50% (art. II s.34a).

instrument_name: Ohio Constitution Article II Section 34a (minimum wage, annual CPI-W indexation)
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage increased each 1 January by CPI-W (all items) inflation for the 12 months before the preceding September (announced 30 September), rounded to nearest 5 cents; under-16 employees and employers with gross receipts at or below the indexed threshold (base 250,000 USD in 2007, rounded to nearest 1,000) at the FLSA rate; tipped employees not less than half the minimum wage. G-DERIVE 2027: 11.00 x 328.481/317.306 (CPI-W Aug 2026/Aug 2025, BLS CWUR0000SA0) = 11.387 -> 11.40; threshold 405,000 x 1.03522 = 419,263 -> 419,000; tipped 11.40/2 = 5.70. All three match the 2027 poster (US-OHS5-004).

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 5747.02 Tax rates (as amended by HB 96, 136th GA)
figure_or_rule_carried: Individual income tax on Ohio AGI less business income and exemptions: balance <= 26,050 USD no tax; TY2024: 360.69 + 2.75% over 26,050 to 100,000, 2,394.32 + 3.5% above; TY2025: 342.00 + 2.75% over 26,050 to 100,000, 2,394.32 + 3.125% above; TY2026 and thereafter: flat 332.00 + 2.75% of the amount over 26,050 (single rate). The withholding tables (US-OH-006, US-OHS5-001) are a separate commissioner rule under 5747.06 and still graduate 1.6%/2.99%/3.4% from 2026-08-01.

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 5747.06 Employer duty to withhold tax
figure_or_rule_carried: Every employer (incl. state and political subdivisions) with an office or transacting business in Ohio withholds each payroll period an amount substantially equivalent to the estimated tax under ch. 5747 and 5748 (school district), on the date compensation is paid or credited; method prescribed by rule of the tax commissioner. No withholding on agricultural labor (IRC 3121(g)); domestic service in a private home, college club or fraternity; service in a quarter with cash pay under 300 USD unless regularly employed; foreign government service; newspaper delivery under 18; non-cash pay outside the trade or business.

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 3121.891 Duty to make a new hire report
figure_or_rule_carried: Every employer reports to ODJFS each newly hired employee or contractor who resides, works or will be assigned to work in Ohio and is expected to be paid; multistate electronic filers may designate one state after notifying ODJFS and HHS in writing. Deadline and fields: see US-OHS5-014 (3121.892).

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 3121.18 Fees (income withholding for support)
figure_or_rule_carried: A payor withholding child support under a 3121.03 notice may deduct from the employee, in addition to support, a fee of the greater of 2 USD or an amount not exceeding 1% of the amount withheld.

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 2329.66(A)(13) Exempt personal earnings (garnishment)
figure_or_rule_carried: Exempt from ordinary creditor garnishment: the greater of (a) 30x the federal minimum hourly wage if paid weekly, 60x biweekly, 65x semimonthly, 130x monthly, or (b) 75% of disposable earnings (support orders excepted via 3119.80/.81, 3121.02/.03, 3123.06). Equivalent to the CCPA floor, with explicit semimonthly (65x) and monthly (130x) multipliers. Federal minimum 7.25 USD.

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 4113.85 Matters subject to employer policy (local preemption of leave and benefit mandates)
figure_or_rule_carried: Except as expressly provided in state or federal law, hours, scheduling, reporting/on-call/split-shift pay and whether and which fringe benefits (incl. leaves of absence, vacation, separation, sick and holiday pay) are provided are exclusively matters of employer policy or agreement; applies to private employers (state and political subdivisions excluded from the employer definition). Basis for: no Ohio paid-sick-leave mandate and no municipal sick-leave or scheduling ordinance binding private employers; vacation payout follows policy.

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 718.01 Definitions - qualifying wages (municipal income tax base)
authority: Ohio General Assembly / LSC (codes.ohio.gov, Wayback copy 2026-06-10)
figure_or_rule_carried: Qualifying wages = IRC 3121(a) wages without wage limitation (Medicare wages), less: section 125 amounts; third-party sick/accident disability pay; NQDC under 3121(v)(2)(C) and stock-option amounts only where the municipality exempted them before 2016-01-01; exempt income; plus pre-1986 Medicare-exempt employment and non-exempted stock-option amounts. Elective 401(k)/403(b) deferrals stay in the base (they are 3121(a) wages).

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 3121.892 (new hire report contents) and 3121.893 (methods and 20-day deadline)
figure_or_rule_carried: Fields: employee name, address, date of birth, SSN, date of hire; contractor name, address, SSN/TIN, date payments begin, expected duration; employer name, address, identification number; ODJFS may add fields by rule. Method as ODJFS prescribes (copy of IRS W-4, ODJFS form or other authorised document/media); mail (postmark date), fax, magnetic or electronic. Deadline: not later than twenty days after the hire (3121.893).

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 4113.15 Semimonthly payment of wages (direct codes.ohio.gov read)
figure_or_rule_carried: Second-family check of US-OH-004 (Wayback copy) on the live official page: wages for the 1st-15th paid on or before the 1st of the next month; for the second half on or before the 15th of the next month; daily or weekly payment allowed; longer customary or contractual lapse allowed. Wages unpaid 30 days beyond the regular payday (60 days where no regular payday) without dispute: liquidated damages. Ohio has no separate final-pay statute: final wages follow this schedule (next regular payday).

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 4141.28 Determination of benefit rights - separating employer and mass layoff notice
figure_or_rule_carried: (B) ODJFS notifies the most recent separating employer of a claim and requests the reason for separation. (C) Mass layoffs: an employer laying off or separating 50 or more individuals in any 7-day period for lack of work notifies the director of dates and approximate number at least 3 working days before the first layoff, and at separation gives each individual and the director the information needed for UI eligibility. No individual separation-notice duty located in this section.

instrument_name: Ohio Administrative Code 5703-7-10 Withholding on supplemental compensation
figure_or_rule_carried: Supplemental compensation = bonuses, commissions and other nonrecurring payments; withheld at the highest rate in ORC 5747.02(A)(3) for the taxable year = 2.75% for TY2026 (US-OHS5-007). Regular pay withheld by pay frequency and the commissioner tables, published by the end of January or within 45 days of a rate change; school district tax withheld at the rate of the employee's district of residence. Confirms US-OH-002 (2.75%, no local file).

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 4141.20 Quarterly contribution and wage report
figure_or_rule_carried: Contributory employers file a quarterly contribution and wage report by the last day of the first month after the quarter: total and taxable remuneration, each employee name and SSN, remuneration per individual, number of weeks paid in the quarter, plus SSA 1137 data. Late or incomplete report: forfeiture 0.25% of total remuneration reported, minimum 50 USD, maximum 1,000 USD. Reimbursing employers file a quarterly payroll and wage report on the same date.

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 1349.19 Security breach notification (private disclosure of personal information)
figure_or_rule_carried: Personal information = name plus unencrypted SSN, driver licence/state ID number, or account/card number with access code. A business discovering a breach that creates material risk of identity theft or fraud discloses it to affected Ohio residents in the most expedient time possible but not later than 45 days after discovery (law-enforcement delay allowed). Applies to payroll data held by the employer or its provider.

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 5747.01(A) Ohio adjusted gross income (federal conformity)
figure_or_rule_carried: Ohio adjusted gross income = federal adjusted gross income as defined in the IRC, with the listed state add-backs/deductions (none of the add-backs read concern 401(k), section 125, HSA, transit or group-term life). State income tax therefore follows the federal exclusions from wages; the municipal base differs (Medicare wages, US-OHS5-013): 401(k)/403(b) deferrals taxable for municipal tax, section 125 excluded. Latest amendment SB 9 (136th GA) effective 2026-03-05.

instrument_name: Ohio Department of Taxation The Finder (address lookup of school district and municipal tax)
article_or_section: lookup tool named by the 2026 filing guidelines (tax.ohio.gov/finder)
figure_or_rule_carried: Official lookup of the school district (four-digit code) and municipal tax for an address; the only official per-address source located for the municipal rate layer (no consolidated municipal rate table could be fetched: tax.ohio.gov HTML returns a 403/404 shell to scripts). Page returned HTTP 200 (application shell); no rates read.
